I am a Principal Economist at the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and previously served as an economist at the Federal Trade Commission and the Department of Justice Antitrust Division. I am an antitrust and competition-policy economist whose research and software translate modern industrial organization models into practical tools for economic analysis. My work focuses on merger review under uncertainty, including market definition, merger simulation, model choice, efficiencies, financial structure, and the use of economic evidence in enforcement and policy.

Banking is an important application of this agenda: it has been central to U.S. merger law since Philadelphia National Bank and provides unusually rich public data for studying how market structure, prices, balance sheets, and local competition shape merger effects. Over nearly two decades of public service, I have led economic investigations and supported high-profile litigations across sectors including retail banking, semiconductors, health insurance, cinema and radio advertising, airlines, and parking services.

## Research and Policy Focus

<div class="impact-grid">
<div class="impact-card">
<h3>Antitrust and Competition Policy</h3>
<p>I study how quantitative models can inform antitrust enforcement and competition policy, with a primary focus on merger review across horizontal, vertical, labor/product, and complex settings.</p>
</div>
<div class="impact-card">
<h3>Open-Source Antitrust and Policy Tools</h3>
<p>I develop software that makes standard antitrust and trade-policy simulation models available in reproducible, practitioner-facing form.</p>
</div>
<div class="impact-card">
<h3>Market Definition and Screening Under Uncertainty</h3>
<p>My work examines how screens, geographic markets, and predicted effects depend on assumptions about conduct, demand, and market boundaries.</p>
</div>
<div class="impact-card">
<h3>Applications to Banking and Regulated Industries</h3>
<p>I apply general antitrust and merger-review tools to banking and regulated markets, using them as key laboratories to study market definition, concentration, and merger effects with rich empirical data.</p>
</div>
</div>
